source_text: Non ergo argui meretur ab Apostolo et a diabolo possidetur; a Deo instituitur, et criminum fons est; a Deo postremo, ut confiteris, benedicitur, et a te frutex diabolicus accusatur.
pass_a_gloss: It is therefore not merited to be accused by the Apostle and is possessed by the devil; it is instituted by God, and is a fountain of crimes; finally it is blessed by God, as you confess, and by you a diabolical shrub is accused.
pass_b_english: So it does not deserve accusation by the apostle, yet is possessed by the devil! It is instituted by God, yet is a fountain of crimes! Finally, it is blessed by God, as you confess, yet accused by you of being the devil’s shrub!

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
